mainTopic: When an uncertain sin requires an אשם תלוי: רב's rule of two pieces versus one piece, רב נחמן's 'established prohibition', and the opposing views of רבי אליעזר and רבי מאיר.
overview: The amud asks when a doubt about a sin requires an אשם תלוי (a provisional guilt offering). First, two sources that seem to go against רבי זירא are answered: each one follows רבי אליעזר. Next, רב teaches that if a person ate one of two pieces, one חלב and one שומן, he brings an אשם תלוי, but a single doubtful piece does not require one. רב נחמן explains that with two pieces the prohibition was 'established.' The גמרא shows how this reason differs from רבא's and רבי זירא's. רבא then challenges רב נחמן three times, and each source is assigned to רבי אליעזר or to רבי מאיר, who do not require an established prohibition. רב then places the case of eating a single doubtful piece inside the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים. רב אשי explains that even רבי אליעזר needs some real doubt. Finally, a ברייתא lists cases of two pieces eaten in different orders, by mistake or on purpose, and by one person or two. The גמרא asks whose view its last ruling follows, and רב אשי's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Objection from the case of the child who may be from either husband
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about a יבמה who gives birth seven months after יבום says that each of them brings an אשם תלוי, which seems to go against רבי זירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: If it is uncertain whether the baby is a nine-month baby from the first husband or a seven-month baby from the second husband, he must divorce her, the child is כשר, and he is obligated in an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא with a ברייתא that requires an אשם תלוי in a case of doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby is from the first husband, the יבמה was pregnant at the time of יבום, so the יבום was forbidden. Since we are not sure, the ברייתא requires an אשם תלוי. That seems to contradict רבי זירא's earlier position, which did not require an אשם תלוי in a case like this.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'hanging' or provisional guilt offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he did a sin that carries כרת
A doubt or uncertainty
He must send her away, meaning divorce her
Of good lineage, not a ממזר

phrases.english: They challenged him: If it is uncertain whether the child is a nine-month child of the first husband
phrases.notes: The case is a יבמה who had יבום and gave birth seven months later. 'Him' is רבי זירא.

phrases.english: or a seven-month child of the latter one
he must divorce her, and the child is of good lineage,
and he is obligated to bring a provisional guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by attacking רבי זירא's position from the previous part of the sugya.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's position that no אשם תלוי is brought in this kind of doubt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא clearly requires an אשם תלוי in a doubt about forbidden relations.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, who requires an אשם תלוי even in such cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי אליעזר's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection by saying the ברייתא follows one specific תנא, רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא was explaining the view of the רבנן. If the ברייתא is רבי אליעזר's view, it does not contradict what רבי זירא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? Used to tie a source to one particular תנא

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Eliezer's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different תנא (רבי אליעזר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is the accepted halacha and goes against רבי זירא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, so רבי זירא's view stands.

steps.title: Objection from blood found after relations
steps.stepSummary: A source about blood found on the woman's cloth some time after relations adds that they are obligated in an אשם תלוי. This is again a challenge to רבי זירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: If blood was found on her cloth right away, they are impure and must bring a קרבן. If it was found after some time, they are impure because of the doubt and exempt from the קרבן. And it was taught about this: they are obligated in an אשם תלוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source that seems to require an אשם תלוי in a case of doubt, against רבי זירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the blood is found after some time, maybe the bleeding began during relations and maybe it began afterward. The משנה itself only exempts them from a חטאת, but the added teaching says they bring an אשם תלוי, which seems to contradict רבי זירא.

keyTerms.meaning: Immediately, right away
Impure because of a doubt
And it was taught about it, an added teaching on the same case
An offering, here a חטאת

phrases.english: They challenged him: If blood was found on hers immediately,
phrases.notes: 'Hers' means the cloth she checks herself with after relations.

phrases.english: they are impure and obligated to bring an offering.
If it was found on hers after some time,
they are impure because of doubt and exempt from the offering.
And it was taught about it: and they are obligated in a provisional guilt offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second objection against the same position of רבי זירא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The added teaching on this משנה requires an אשם תלוי in a doubt about forbidden relations.

steps.title: This source also follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: Again the גמרא answers that this follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי אליעזר's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before: this source is רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added teaching that requires an אשם תלוי matches רבי אליעזר and not the רבנן. So רבי זירא, who was explaining the רבנן, is not contradicted.
steps.whatToRemember: Both objections are answered the same way: sources that require an אשם תלוי in these doubtful cases follow רבי אליעזר, so רבי זירא's view of the רבנן stands.

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Eliezer's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 3 the same way step 2 answered step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different תנא (רבי אליעזר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The added teaching goes against רבי זירא.
steps.terutzMaskana: It follows רבי אליעזר, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: רב's rule: two pieces versus one piece
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that eating one of two pieces, one חלב and one שומן, requires an אשם תלוי. Eating a single piece that might be חלב does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה in the name of רב: If there were two pieces in front of him, one of חלב and one of שומן, and he ate one of them and does not know which one he ate, he is obligated. If there was one piece that might be חלב and might be שומן, and he ate it, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. רב teaches when a doubt about eating forbidden fat requires an אשם תלוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the person is unsure whether he ate חלב. The difference is the setup: with two pieces, one of them was definitely forbidden. With a single piece, maybe there was never any חלב at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat. Eating it on purpose is punished with כרת
Permitted fat
A piece
Obligated, here to bring an אשם תלוי
Exempt

steps.confusionAlert: In both cases the person does not know whether he ate חלב. The difference is not how strong the doubt is. It is whether a definitely forbidden piece was in front of him to begin with.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the famous rule of 'חתיכה משתי חתיכות': the case of one piece out of two is the classic case where an אשם תלוי is brought.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said that Rav said:
If there were two pieces before him,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל חֵלֶב וְאַחַת שֶׁל שׁוּמָּן,
phrases.english: one of forbidden fat and one of permitted fat,
and he ate one of them

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ אֵיזוֹ מֵהֶן אָכַל – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: and he does not know which of them he ate, he is obligated.

phrases.aramaic: חֲתִיכָה, סָפֵק שֶׁל חֵלֶב סָפֵק שֶׁל שׁוּמָּן
phrases.english: A single piece, maybe of forbidden fat, maybe of permitted fat,
and he ate it, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement about the conditions for an אשם תלוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating one of two pieces, one of which was חלב, requires an אשם תלוי. Eating a single piece that may or may not be חלב does not.

steps.title: רב נחמן asks for רב's reason
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks why רב makes a difference between two pieces and one piece.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: What is the reason for רב's view?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן asks a question that sets up his explanation of רב's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the person might have eaten חלב, so it is not obvious why they should be different. רב נחמן wants the logic behind the distinction.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב?
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said: What is the reason of Rav?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רב's ruling in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רב makes the two-piece case obligated and the one-piece case exempt.

steps.title: With two pieces the prohibition was established
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains: with two pieces, the prohibition was definitely present. With one piece, it was never established.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: with two pieces, the prohibition was established. With one piece, the prohibition was not established.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers his own question by explaining רב's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When there are two pieces, there was definitely חלב in front of him, and the only doubt is which piece he ate. With one piece, we never knew there was any חלב there at all. An אשם תלוי is only brought when the prohibition was clearly present.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, meaning this is his reasoning
The prohibition was established, meaning a forbidden item was definitely there

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, as רב נחמן explains him, an אשם תלוי needs a 'fixed' prohibition: one piece out of two, where one was surely חלב. A lone doubtful piece does not require one. Later steps show that רבי אליעזר and רבי מאיר disagree.

phrases.english: He holds: with two pieces, the prohibition was established,
with one piece, the prohibition was not established.
phrases.notes: Some versions say קבעה, the word in round brackets. The corrected wording, in square brackets, is איקבע, to match the first half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With two pieces there was a definite prohibition present, so an אשם תלוי is needed. With one piece there was no definite prohibition, so he is exempt.

steps.title: Is there any difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רב נחמן's reason, that the prohibition was established, and רבי זירא's reason, that the prohibition cannot be identified.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between saying 'the prohibition was established' and saying 'it is impossible to identify its prohibition'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now has two explanations for why רב requires two pieces, and it asks whether they ever lead to different results. This question sets up the next step, which gives a case where they differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said one piece is exempt because there is nothing to compare it with, so you can never clear up the doubt. רב נחמן said two pieces are liable because a forbidden piece was definitely there. In most cases both reasons give the same result, so the גמרא wants a case that separates them.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between? The standard way the גמרא asks for the practical difference between two reasons.
The prohibition was established, meaning a forbidden item was definitely present.
To identify its prohibition, meaning to find out which item was the forbidden one.

phrases.english: What difference is there between 'the prohibition was established'
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן's reason from the previous step.

phrases.english: and 'it is impossible to identify its prohibition'?
phrases.notes: This is רבי זירא's reason, given earlier on the daf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב נחמן gives his reason, the גמרא compares it with רבי זירא's reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where 'the prohibition was established' and 'the prohibition cannot be identified' lead to different rulings.

steps.title: The case of the non-Jew eating the first piece
steps.stepSummary: The difference shows up when a non-Jew eats one of the two pieces and then a Jew eats the other. רבא and רבי זירא exempt the Jew. רב נחמן holds him liable for an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them. Suppose two pieces were in front of someone, one of forbidden fat and one of permitted fat. A non-Jew came and ate the first, and then a Jew came and ate the second. According to רבא, there are no 'מצות' (two items) at the moment the Jew ate. According to רבי זירא, it is impossible to identify the prohibition. According to רב נחמן, the prohibition was established.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a case. Two pieces start out together, but by the time the Jew eats, only one is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, what matters is that two pieces are present at the moment of eating, and here there was only one, so the Jew is exempt. For רבי זירא, the other piece is gone, so the doubt can never be cleared up, and he too exempts. For רב נחמן, a forbidden piece was definitely there at some point, so the Jew is liable to bring an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them. This introduces the practical case.
Commandments, a plural word in the פסוק. רבא learns from it that two items must be present.
At the time, at the moment.
Permitted fat.

steps.whatToRemember: This case is the test: רבא and רבי זירא exempt, while רב נחמן obligates an אשם תלוי, because for him it is enough that the forbidden piece was once definitely there.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the non-Jew's eating is a sin. He simply takes one piece away, so only one piece is left when the Jew eats.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
in a case where two pieces were before him,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל חֵלֶב וְאַחַת שֶׁל שׁוּמָּן,
phrases.english: one of forbidden fat and one of permitted fat,
and a non-Jew came and ate the first,
and a Jew came and ate the second.
According to רבא, there are no 'מצות' (two items)
phrases.notes: רבא reads the plural word מצות in the פסוק (ויקרא 5:17) as requiring two items in front of the person.

phrases.english: at the moment the Jew ate.

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי זֵירָא – אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְבָרֵר אִיסּוּרֵיהּ.
phrases.english: According to רבי זירא, it is impossible to identify its prohibition.
According to רב נחמן, the prohibition was established.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by giving a case that separates the opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When a non-Jew eats the first piece and a Jew eats the second, רבא and רבי זירא exempt the Jew, but רב נחמן obligates him because the prohibition was once established.

steps.title: Challenge from a כוי
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן: רבי אליעזר obligates an אשם תלוי for eating the fat of a כוי, even though the prohibition was never established.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised an objection to רב נחמן. רבי אליעזר says: for a כוי, one is liable to bring an אשם תלוי for its fat!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's reason using a ruling about a כוי, an animal whose status is in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a כוי there is only one piece of fat, and no one ever knew for sure that forbidden fat was there. Yet an אשם תלוי is required. That goes against רב נחמן, who says the prohibition must first be established.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal of doubtful status. It is unclear whether it counts as a wild animal or a domestic one.
Its fat. If the animal counts as domestic, this fat is forbidden.

phrases.english: רבא raised an objection to רב נחמן:
רבי אליעזר says:

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹי – חַיָּיבִין עַל חֶלְבּוֹ אָשָׁם תָּלוּי!
phrases.english: For a כוי, one is liable to bring an אשם תלוי for its fat!
phrases.notes: The fat of a wild animal is permitted and the fat of a domestic animal is forbidden, so a כוי's fat is a doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רב נחמן's view is clear, רבא attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule that an אשם תלוי requires the prohibition to have been established
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כוי is a single doubtful item where the prohibition was never definitely present, yet an אשם תלוי is still required.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר does not need an established prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רבי אליעזר does not require the prohibition to be established, so his ruling does not challenge רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר does not require the prohibition to be established.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's challenge: the source follows רבי אליעזר's own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already saw that רבי אליעזר obligates an אשם תלוי even without two pieces. רב נחמן follows the other view, which does require an established prohibition, so רבי אליעזר's ruling does not apply to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Establishment. Here it means that the prohibition was definitely present.
Does not require.

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר does not require
that the prohibition be established.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לָא בָּעֵי קְבִיעוּתָא לְאִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different opinion (רבי אליעזר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כוי ruling seemed to show that everyone obligates an אשם תלוי without an established prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only רבי אליעזר holds that way. רב נחמן follows the view that requires an established prohibition.

steps.title: Challenge from the doubtful birth after יבום
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges again: when a baby born after יבום may belong to either husband, an אשם תלוי is required, even though no prohibition was ever established.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised another objection. If there is doubt whether the child is a nine-month baby of the first husband or a seven-month baby of the later one, he must divorce her, the child is of good lineage, and they are liable to bring an אשם תלוי!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a second source against רב נחמן, this time about a woman who did יבום and then gave birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby is from the first husband, the brother left a child, so there was no מצוה of יבום and the relations were forbidden. If the baby is from the second husband, everything was permitted. This is one single doubt that was never established as a prohibition, yet an אשם תלוי is required, which goes against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby born after nine months of pregnancy.
A baby born after seven months of pregnancy.
He must divorce her (literally, send her out).
The child is of good lineage, not a ממזר.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
If there is a doubt whether the child is a nine-month baby of the first husband,
phrases.notes: The woman did יבום soon after her husband died, and the baby came seven months later.

phrases.english: or a seven-month baby of the later husband,
he must divorce her, and the child is of good lineage,
and they are liable to bring an אשם תלוי!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against רב נחמן, following the same pattern as the first.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule that an אשם תלוי requires an established prohibition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The doubtful-birth case involves a single doubt, with no prohibition ever definitely present, yet it still requires an אשם תלוי.

steps.title: This source also follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this ruling also follows רבי אליעזר, so it does not challenge רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי אליעזר's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge the same way it answered the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because רבי אליעזר does not need an established prohibition, any source that requires an אשם תלוי for a lone doubt can be assigned to him. רב נחמן's position stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this? Used to assign a source to a specific תנא.

steps.whatToRemember: Both sources that require an אשם תלוי without an established prohibition (the כוי and the doubtful birth) follow רבי אליעזר. רב נחמן's rule stands, because he follows the view that disagrees with רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?
It is רבי אליעזר's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second challenge using the same idea as step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different opinion (רבי אליעזר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubtful-birth ruling seemed to show that everyone obligates an אשם תלוי without an established prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling follows רבי אליעזר, who does not require an established prohibition.

steps.title: רבא's final challenge: blood found after time passed
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן from a משנה. When blood is found on the woman's cloth some time after relations, the couple must still bring an אשם תלוי, even though no prohibition was ever established.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised an objection: If blood is found on his cloth, they are both impure and must bring a חטאת. If it is found on her cloth right away, they are impure and must bring a חטאת. If it is found on her cloth after some time, they are impure because of the doubt and exempt from the חטאת. And a ברייתא adds about this case: they must bring an אשם תלוי!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings one more source against רב נחמן. In the last case of this משנה, nobody knows whether a sin happened, yet an אשם תלוי is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the 'after time passed' case there is only one act with a single doubt: maybe she was already bleeding during relations, maybe not. There was never a definite prohibition sitting beside it, the way a definite piece of חלב sits beside the doubtful one. Even so, the ברייתא requires an אשם תלוי, which seems to go against רב נחמן's demand for an established prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually impure (here, for seven days, like a נִדָּה)
Immediately, right away
After some time has passed
Impure because of a doubt
And a ברייתא was taught about it (adding to the משנה)

phrases.english: He (רבא) raised an objection to him:

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא עַל שֶׁלּוֹ – טְמֵאִין וְחַיָּיבִין בַּקׇּרְבָּן,
phrases.english: If blood was found on his cloth, they are impure and liable to bring an offering;
phrases.notes: The couple checked with cloths after relations. If blood is on his cloth, she was definitely bleeding during relations.

phrases.english: if it was found on her cloth immediately,
they are impure and liable to bring an offering;
if it was found on her cloth after some time,
they are impure because of the doubt and exempt from the offering.
And it was taught about this: and they are liable to bring a provisional guilt offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third challenge in רבא's series, after the cases of the כוי and the baby born after יבום.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's position that an אשם תלוי requires the prohibition to be established
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the 'after time passed' case there is only a single doubtful act with no definite prohibition, yet the ברייתא requires an אשם תלוי.

steps.title: רב נחמן's answer after רבא left: it follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן did not answer at the time. After רבא left, he said he should have answered that this ruling follows רבי מאיר, who does not require an established prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was silent. After רבא left, he said: Why didn't I tell him that this follows רבי מאיר, who does not require the prohibition to be established?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן could not answer on the spot. Later he gives the answer he should have given: the ruling follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן says the ברייתא requiring an אשם תלוי follows רבי מאיר. רבי מאיר does not need an established prohibition before requiring an אשם תלוי. So the ruling does not disprove רב נחמן, whose view follows the opinion that does require it.

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent (he had no answer at the moment)
After he left
Whose opinion is it?
An established prohibition, meaning a definite forbidden item is known to be in the picture

phrases.english: He (רב נחמן) was silent.
After he (רבא) left, he said:
Why didn't I say to him
that this ruling, whose is it? It is רבי מאיר's,
who does not require the prohibition to be established?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אֲמַרִי לֵיהּ דְּהָא מַנִּי רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to show that everyone requires an אשם תלוי even without an established prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who does not require קביעותא, so it is no challenge to רב נחמן.

steps.title: Proof of רבי מאיר's view: slaughtering an אשם תלוי outside
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר requires an אשם תלוי even without an established prohibition. He obligates someone who slaughters an אשם תלוי outside the Temple, and the חכמים exempt him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: One who slaughters an אשם תלוי outside the Temple: רבי מאיר holds him liable, and the חכמים exempt him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that shows רבי מאיר really holds this view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original owner of an אשם תלוי may never have sinned at all. If so, the animal was never truly holy, and slaughtering it outside was never truly forbidden. רבי מאיר still holds the slaughterer liable for an אשם תלוי, which shows he does not require an established prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering a קרבן outside the Temple, which is forbidden
Holds him liable
Exempt him

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the proof that רבי מאיר's opinion really exists, so the answer in step 15 is not just a guess.

phrases.english: As it was taught: One who slaughters a provisional guilt offering outside the Temple:
רבי מאיר holds him liable, and the Rabbis exempt him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 15 that רבי מאיר does not require קביעותא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר does not require an established prohibition for an אשם תלוי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about slaughtering an אשם תלוי outside the Temple

steps.title: Why not just say רבי אליעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב נחמן named רבי מאיר. The earlier challenges were answered by saying the ruling follows רבי אליעזר, so why not say the same here?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let him say to him that it follows רבי אליעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב נחמן needed a new name, רבי מאיר. It is setting up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 11 and 13, the answer was that רבי אליעזר does not require an established prohibition. That same easy answer seems to work here too, so bringing in רבי מאיר looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Let him say to him (he could have answered...)

phrases.english: But why?
Let him say to him that it follows רבי אליעזר!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי לֵימָא לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the choice of רבי מאיר in the answer of steps 15–16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב נחמן named רבי מאיר instead of רבי אליעזר, who was used for the earlier answers

steps.title: רבי מאיר follows רבי אליעזר's approach
steps.stepSummary: By naming רבי מאיר, רב נחמן teaches something new: רבי מאיר holds like רבי אליעזר on this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he teaches us: that רבי מאיר holds like רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that mentioning רבי מאיר adds new information. רבי מאיר follows רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'רבי אליעזר' would only have repeated what we already knew. Naming רבי מאיר teaches that a second תנא also holds that an אשם תלוי does not require an established prohibition. Both opinions stand against רב נחמן's view, but neither one disproves it.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he is teaching us
Stands in the approach of רבי אליעזר (holds like him)

steps.whatToRemember: All three challenges from רבא are answered the same way. Each source follows רבי אליעזר or רבי מאיר, who do not require an established prohibition (קביעותא לאיסורא) for an אשם תלוי. רב נחמן follows the view that does require it, so none of these sources disproves him.

phrases.english: This is what he is teaching us:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר קָאֵי.
phrases.english: that רבי מאיר holds in line with the approach of רבי אליעזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Naming רבי מאיר teaches the new point that he shares רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר both hold that an אשם תלוי does not need an established prohibition. רב נחמן's view stands.

steps.title: One uncertain piece brings us to a known dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה quotes רב: if someone ate a single piece that might be חלב or might be שומן, this is exactly the מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר אבוה said in the name of רב: If there was one piece, and we don't know if it is forbidden fat or permitted fat, and someone ate it, we have reached the argument between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a statement from רב. Eating one piece of uncertain fat is a case that רבי אליעזר and the חכמים argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there was only one piece, so there was never a clear pair of 'one forbidden, one permitted' to choose from. רב places this case inside the מחלוקת: רבי אליעזר is lenient about bringing an אשם תלוי, and the חכמים want a real case of doubt about a sin.

keyTerms.meaning: A piece (here, a piece of fat)
Forbidden fat. Eating it on purpose is כרת, and by mistake it requires a חטאת
Permitted fat
A doubt; something uncertain
A dispute between sages

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Avuh said that Rav said:
A piece, uncertain whether it is of forbidden fat
or uncertain whether it is of permitted fat, and he ate it,
we have arrived at the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages.
phrases.notes: This is the argument in the משנה on 25a about whether a person may bring an אשם תלוי whenever he wants.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section about a single piece of uncertain status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single piece of doubtful חלב that was eaten falls under the מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and the חכמים.

steps.title: Why did רב need the person to eat it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: for רבי אליעזר, eating should not matter, since he lets a person volunteer an אשם תלוי every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, why does it matter that he ate it? Even if he didn't eat anything, he could bring one! We learned that רבי אליעזר says a person may volunteer an אשם תלוי every single day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's wording. If רבי אליעזר lets someone bring an אשם תלוי with no doubt at all, why did רב build a case where the person ate something?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is on the detail 'and he ate it.' For רבי אליעזר, an אשם תלוי seems to need no reason at all, so eating an uncertain piece should add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case?
Brings voluntarily, as a donation
A provisional guilt offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he sinned

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, מַאי אִירְיָא כִּי אַכְלַהּ?
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Eliezer, why specifically when he ate it?
Even if he did not eat it, the same should be true!
For we learned in a mishna: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: מִתְנַדֵּב אָדָם אָשָׁם תָּלוּי בְּכׇל יוֹם!
phrases.english: A person may volunteer a provisional guilt offering every day!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, מַאי אִירְיָא כִּי אַכְלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the 'he ate it' detail in רב's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's case requiring that the person ate the uncertain piece.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר allows a voluntary אשם תלוי every day, so for him eating should not be needed.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר follows בבא בן בוטא: wait for a real doubt
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that רב means רבי אליעזר as he fits בבא בן בוטא's story, where the sages told בבא בן בוטא to wait until he was in a real situation of doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: רב means רבי אליעזר's view as it fits with בבא בן בוטא. We learned that they told בבא בן בוטא: Wait until you are in a situation of doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why eating matters even for רבי אליעזר. Bringing the offering still needs some real doubt, like eating a piece that might be חלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same משנה tells that בבא בן בוטא wanted to bring an אשם תלוי every day, even the day after יום כיפור. He was told to wait until he 'enters a situation of doubt.' So רבי אליעזר is read as allowing the offering for even a small doubt, like one uncertain piece, but not for no doubt at all.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of
Wait
A situation of doubt

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי אליעזר's 'every day' as 'for no reason at all.' According to רב אשי, there still has to be some real doubt, even a small one.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אַלִּיבָּא דְּבָבָא בֶּן בּוּטָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer according to the view of Bava ben Buta,
as we learned in a mishna: But they say to him:
phrases.notes: This is from the story where בבא בן בוטא wanted to bring an אשם תלוי every day.

phrases.english: Wait until you enter into a situation of doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אַלִּיבָּא דְּבָבָא בֶּן בּוּטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about why eating was needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the view: רבי אליעזר is read the way בבא בן בוטא's story shows it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר allows an אשם תלוי with no doubt at all, so eating is irrelevant.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even for רבי אליעזר there must be some situation of doubt, so the eating of an uncertain piece matters.
steps.whatToRemember: Even for רבי אליעזר, an אשם תלוי needs some real situation of doubt. Eating one uncertain piece is enough for him.

steps.title: Two pieces: the Jew eats first, someone else eats second
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: there were two pieces, one שומן and one חלב. A Jew ate the first, then a גוי ate the second. The Jew is חייב. The same is true if a dog or a raven ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: There were two pieces in front of him, one permitted fat and one forbidden fat. A Jew came and ate the first one, then a non-Jew came and ate the second one. The Jew is obligated. The same is true if a dog or a raven ate the second one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with two pieces, one forbidden and one permitted. If the Jew eats first, he must bring an אשם תלוי, no matter who eats the other piece afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the Jew ate, both pieces were still there. So his doubt came from a classic pair of 'one forbidden, one permitted.' What happens to the second piece later doesn't change that.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligated (here, to bring an אשם תלוי)
Dog
Raven

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שְׁתֵּי חֲתִיכוֹת,
phrases.english: The Sages taught: There were two pieces before him,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל שׁוּמָּן וְאַחַת שֶׁל חֵלֶב,
phrases.english: one of permitted fat and one of forbidden fat;
a Jew came and ate the first one,

phrases.aramaic: בָּא גּוֹי וְאָכַל אֶת הַשְּׁנִיָּה – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: then a gentile came and ate the second one: he is liable,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the Jew, who must bring an אשם תלוי.

phrases.english: and the same if a dog ate it, and the same if a raven ate it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שְׁתֵּי חֲתִיכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא about two pieces of fat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the Jew eats first while both pieces are present, he is חייב an אשם תלוי, even if a גוי or an animal eats the other piece.

steps.title: Reverse order: the גוי eats first, and רבי disagrees
steps.stepSummary: If the גוי ate first and the Jew ate the second piece, the Jew is פטור. רבי makes him חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a non-Jew came and ate the first one, and then a Jew came and ate the second one, the Jew is exempt. רבי says he is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now flips the order. The first view exempts the Jew, and רבי argues and obligates him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the Jew ate, only one piece was left, so his doubt came from a single piece, not from a pair. The first view needs two pieces present at the time of eating. רבי does not need two pieces, so for him one doubtful piece is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt
Holds that he is obligated

steps.whatToRemember: What counts is how many pieces were there when the Jew ate. Two pieces make him חייב. Once only one piece is left, the first view says פטור and רבי says חייב.

phrases.english: If a gentile came and ate the first one,

phrases.aramaic: בָּא יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָכַל אֶת הַשְּׁנִיָּה – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: and then a Jew came and ate the second one, he is exempt.
And Rabbi deems him obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse order of the same ברייתא, with רבי's dissent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under the first view, a Jew who eats the last remaining piece is פטור. רבי obligates him.

steps.title: Mixing mistake and on-purpose eating of the two pieces
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. First by mistake and second on purpose means חייב. First on purpose and second by mistake means פטור, but רבי says חייב. Both on purpose means פטור from everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate the first piece by mistake and the second on purpose, he is liable. If he ate the first on purpose and the second by mistake, he is exempt, and רבי makes him liable. If he ate both on purpose, he is exempt from everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 22 keeps listing cases. Now it looks at what happens when the person ate one piece by mistake (שוגג) and one on purpose (מזיד).
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם תלוי only comes for a mistake, and the question is whether two pieces were there when the mistake happened. If the mistaken eating came first, both pieces were still there, so he is חייב. If the mistaken eating came second, only one piece was left, so the חכמים say פטור, just like in step 23, while רבי still says חייב. Eating on purpose never brings a קרבן, so eating both on purpose means פטור מכלום.

keyTerms.meaning: by mistake, without knowing
on purpose, knowingly
exempt from bringing anything at all

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the on-purpose eating makes him more liable. A קרבן is only for a mistake, so the on-purpose eating simply 'uses up' a piece without bringing any קרבן.

phrases.english: If he ate the first one by mistake,
and the second on purpose – he is liable.
phrases.notes: Liable for an אשם תלוי because of the first piece, when both pieces were still there.

phrases.english: The first on purpose, and the second by mistake –
he is exempt, and רבי holds him liable.
If he ate both of them on purpose – he is exempt from everything.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָכַל אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה בְּשׁוֹגֵג, וְהַשְּׁנִיָּה בְּמֵזִיד – חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, adding cases where one eating was by mistake and the other on purpose.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם תלוי comes only for a mistaken eating done while both pieces were present. According to the חכמים, a mistaken eating of the lone remaining piece is פטור, while רבי says חייב. Eating on purpose brings nothing.

steps.title: Two people each eat one piece by mistake
steps.stepSummary: If two people each ate one piece by mistake, both are חייב. The second is obligated not from the דין, but because exempting him would lock the first person into a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If both ate by mistake, both are liable. The second one is not liable by the strict law. It is only because if you say he is exempt, you have set the first one as owing a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a case of two different people, each eating one of the two pieces by mistake. It says both bring an אשם תלוי, but it gives the second person a special reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first person ate while two pieces were there, so he is truly in doubt and brings an אשם תלוי. The second person ate when only one piece was left, so strictly he would be פטור. But if we exempt him, it looks as if his piece was the permitted one. That would mean the first person surely ate the חלב and must bring a real חטאת. So the second person is made חייב to avoid that wrong conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: by the strict law
you have fixed / established for certain
a sin offering, brought when one surely did the sin by mistake

phrases.english: Both of them by mistake –
phrases.notes: Here two different people each ate one piece.

phrases.english: both of them are liable.
The second one is not liable by the strict law,
but because if you say he is exempt –
you have fixed the first one as owing a sin offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final case of the same ברייתא, moving from one person to two people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two people each eat one piece by mistake, both bring an אשם תלוי. The second does so not by strict law, but so the first is not established as owing a חטאת.
steps.whyThisMatters: The odd phrase 'not from the דין' is exactly what the גמרא is about to question.

steps.title: Whose view is this ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view this is. For רבי, the second person is liable by full דין. For the רבנן, we would be telling him to bring חולין לעזרה just to protect the first person. רב אשי begins to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If it is רבי, it is fully by law! If it is the רבנן, should we tell the second one, just so that the first is not fixed as owing a חטאת, to bring an unconsecrated animal into the Temple courtyard?! רב אשי said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last line of the ברייתא from both sides: it doesn't fit רבי and it doesn't fit the רבנן. At the end, רב אשי starts to give an answer, which continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that even a doubt about one piece brings an אשם תלוי, so for him the second person is חייב by real דין, not 'not from the דין.' The רבנן hold that one piece brings no אשם תלוי, so the second person's animal would not really be a קרבן. Slaughtering a non-holy animal in the עזרה is forbidden, so how can we make him do that just for a side reason?

keyTerms.meaning: and who is it? (whose opinion is this?)
non-holy animals brought into the Temple courtyard, which is forbidden
bring!

phrases.english: And whose view is this?

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי – מִן הַדִּין וּמִן הַדִּין הוּא!
phrases.english: If it is רבי – it is fully by the strict law!
phrases.notes: Literally, 'it is from the law and from the law.' רבי obligates even for one piece, as in step 23.

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבָּנַן – מִשּׁוּם דְּלֹא נִקְבַּע רִאשׁוֹן בְּחַטָּאת,
phrases.english: If it is the Rabbis – just so the first is not fixed as owing a sin offering,
should we say to the second one:
Bring a non-holy animal into the Temple courtyard?!
רב אשי said:

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַנּוּ? אִי רַבִּי – מִן הַדִּין וּמִן הַדִּין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'not from the דין' reasoning of step 25 by showing it fits neither רבי nor the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that the second person is obligated 'not from the דין' only to avoid fixing the first in a חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי, the obligation is a real דין, so 'not from the דין' is wrong. For the רבנן, there is no real obligation, so his animal would be חולין לעזרה, which can't be allowed just to protect someone else.
